thread:
maria: Heads up — after the v2.3.7 canary rolled at ~1755554280 we're seeing a sharp uptick in 5xxs on /v1/generate across canary nodes (error rate ~9-12% over the last 2 mins). Investigating now.

ashok: saw the spike too. traces show most 500s have a tokenizer error in the stack: 
```
Error: TokenizationError: invalid token at offset 1024
 at Tokenizer.process (/srv/runtime/tokenizer.js:214:15)
```
Appears tied to the new tokenizer changes in commit abc1234.

incident-bot: Paging @sre-oncall for SEV2 — Canary 5xx spike during v2.3.7 rollout (thread: 1755554321). Use /incidents handoff when oncall.

sre-oncall: I'm oncall and joining. Thanks for the signal, @maria @ashok. Can you confirm which commit landed the tokenizer change?

maria: commit abc1234 pushed as part of the canary. It's a single small tokenizer refactor. Canary population is 5%.

joel: quick triage — if it's that commit, we can either toggle the tokenizer feature-flag off or revert that single commit and redeploy the canary. Which is faster?

ashok: toggle flag would be fastest if the change was behind a flag. This refactor was rolled unflagged, so flag won't help. Revert single commit and redeploy canary is the likely path.

support-lead: Customer page hits: a handful of hosted API calls saw 500s but we don't yet see billing/chargebacks. A couple customers in EU reported degraded responses. Putting a short note to affected accounts (internal).

sre-oncall: Plan then — revert the single commit (git revert abc1234), build, deploy to canary, monitor for 5xxs, then promote. If that looks good, roll to prod. I'll coordinate the handoff. @deploy-bot can you gate a canary-only deploy?

deploy-bot: Received revert request. Triggering canary deploy pipeline with rollback commit (revert-abc1234). Canaries: 5% traffic retention.

ashok: I'll create the revert PR now. Patch is tiny.

ashok: PR created and merged: revert abc1234 -> commit def5678. Build kicked off.

deploy-bot: Build 459 started for revert patch.

maria: throwing in a quick health-check dashboard snippet — watch 5xx rate, p50/p95 latency, and tokenization-error logs.

sre-oncall: Build passed. Deploying canary (revert) now.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started (build 459). Rolling to nodes: node-a,node-b,node-c.

ashok: adding emergency step — if canary doesn't stabilize in 3 mins, we'll flip the kill-switch for the entire tokenizer pipeline and failover to fallback tokenizer. Command to flip in ops-console: "feature.tokenizer_v2.enabled = false".

joel: noted. Let's also prepare a hotfix release if revert fails. But revert should be straightforward; it's a single commit.

(90s later)

deploy-bot: Canary health: node-a OK, node-b OK, node-c OK. 5xx rate dropped to ~0.4%.

maria: looks stable from logs. TokenizationError entries gone.

support-lead: Customer-facing impact resolved for those who reported. Notifying the small set we emailed.

sre-oncall: Good. I'll keep the revert canary in for 15 min before promoting. Creating incident ticket and scheduling postmortem.

ashok: Created incident ticket INC-2026-104 and postmortem draft in /incidents/posts/INC-2026-104.md. Root cause flagged: unguarded tokenizer refactor (no canary-specific tests).

joel: follow-up actions: (1) add tokenizer unit tests with edge-case inputs, (2) ensure any tokenizer refactor is behind a feature flag, (3) add canary synthetic with long-token inputs.

maria: +1. Also let's add a quick regression alert that watches for TokenizationError spike during rollouts.

sre-oncall: Handing back to normal rotation in 10m. If anyone sees a secondary spike, re-open this thread. Great job everyone. :tada:

incident-bot: Incident state updated to RESOLVED (SEV2) by sre-oncall. Timeline and minutes attached in INC-2026-104.

support-lead: Closing customer notification loop — all affected accounts updated.

joel: Postmortem scheduled tomorrow 11:00 PT.

maria: Thanks team. Leaving the canary revert in prod for now; we'll promote once postmortem actions are in flight.

sre-oncall: last check — no outstanding alerts. Closing thread.
